title: Mondriaanhuis website
lede: The museum in Mondrian’s birthplace in Amersfoort frames its photographs with offset black lines and uses flat yellow buttons and gray-blue planes.
summary: Offset black line frames around photos, flat yellow buttons, a gray-blue plane, and capitals in the navigation.

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 and inspected. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens. The request redirected to the Dutch home page, https://www.mondriaanhuis.nl/nl/.

styles.note: Borderline: the logo and photographs are framed by offset black horizontal and vertical lines, and the buttons are flat yellow, but the lines are thin, photographs dominate, and there is no red or blue plane.

observed: The logo is a rectangle of black lines that overlap and extend past their corners, with a small gray-blue plane and the words AMERSFOORT and MONDRIAANHUIS in capitals.
The navigation is set in small letter-spaced capitals: PLAN JE BEZOEK, ZIEN EN DOEN, OVER HET MONDRIAANHUIS, TICKETS.
Two flat yellow buttons with square corners read “Koop Tickets” and “Webshop”.
A news panel in gray-blue overlaps a photograph of a museum room; thin dark lines run along and past the edges of the photographs.
A large photograph shows a canal street in Amersfoort with the text “Ontdek Piet Mondriaan in zijn geboortehuis”.
interpretation: The site quotes the style through lines that run past their corners, as in Mondrian’s paintings, and through flat yellow, but it is mostly a photograph-led museum site.
Measured: 3 px median border, 3 hues, 0.24 uppercase share, and no rounded corners; the chromatic share is 0.04 because photographs and white dominate.
borrow: Frame an image or a logo with black lines that overshoot the corners instead of a closed box.

images.alt: Museum home page with a logo framed by overlapping black lines, capitalized navigation, two flat yellow buttons, a gray-blue news panel overlapping a photograph of a museum room, and a large photograph of a canal street.
